- The pairs used ours = B in every pair, as fixed. My A/B judgement is therefore not truly blind; I judged each pair on the frames themselves.. Judge: A wins all four pairs clearly, and none were close enough to call indistinguishable. The A frames build depth in layers, with dense, weathered detail at every scale. They use strong sun-driven lighting and haze: lens flare, aerial perspective and long shadows. They also have cinematic subjects, such as the banking helicopter, the hero walk and the hillside-sign overlook. The B frames are a recognizable Singapore-style waterfront: the landmark layout reads well, pair 1 has a real crowd and pair 4 is ambitious in scale. But B looks pre-alpha in the same ways every time. Large near-field surfaces are empty: plain plaza slabs, blank walls and bare roofs. Materials are flat: matte unreflective glass, untextured or tiled facades, and smooth white landmark shapes. Assets repeat (identical palms, trees and box towers). Lighting is diffuse and low in contrast, with weak shadows and haze that does not grade with depth. Hero subjects are weak (a tiny backlit helicopter, a stiff idle character), and the HUD takes about 20% of the frame. In order of impact, the fixes are: (1) dense near-field dressing and ground-floor street detail; (2) believable glazing with reflections, mullion depth and storefronts; (3) a low, directional sun with long shadows and haze that fades with distance; (4) presenting the hero vehicle and character better. Two caveats about this test. The A frames look like curated marketing shots and the B frames are gameplay captures, so some of the composition gap comes from shot selection, though the material, lighting and density gaps are real. More importantly, the blinding broke: pair-2 A and pair-3 A carry a visible publisher logo watermark, and every B gameplay frame carries a distinctive HUD. Future runs should crop or mask logos and either hide the HUD or show it on both sides. I judged visual quality only, read nothing beyond the 12 provided files, and used Bash only for date -u.
